issues.description: Image bytes are pushed downstream without decoding to a raw RGB buffer, corrupting the frame contract
issues.detail: PIL's Image.open returns an image in whatever mode the source encodes (often RGBA, P, or even mode 'L'). Calling image.tobytes() yields bytes in that mode while the frame is declared format='RGB'. The postcondition 'buffer matches declared format' is violated. The author must convert: image = image.convert('RGB') before tobytes(). UNREASONED.

issues.description: Monkey-patching a private module attribute at import time is a smuggled global side effect
issues.detail: genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 5*1024*1024 mutates a private symbol of a third-party library at module import. Precondition (the attribute exists, name is stable across versions) is unstated; postcondition (any other consumer of genai in the same process inherits this buffer) is unexamined. Labeled 'Temporary hack' yet shipped. DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE and SMUGGLED-GOTO into another module's state.

issues.description: Image-model detection by substring 'image' in model name is a fragile invariant
issues.detail: _maybe_unset_thinking_budget now branches on `"image" in self._model_name`. The invariant 'model is an image-generation model iff its name contains image' is asserted by coincidence of current naming, not by any specification from the SDK. A future model named gemini-3-image-aware or gemini-vision-image will silently break the budget logic. Make the predicate explicit.

issues.description: Silent default-model change is an undocumented breaking precondition shift
issues.detail: Default model moved from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash. Every caller that relied on the prior default now silently changes behavior, pricing, latency, and thinking-budget defaults. The CHANGELOG mentions it; the constructor signature does not warn. Existing user code is the precondition; you have changed it without a deprecation step.

issues.description: No termination or size bound on inline image data; OOM is reachable
issues.detail: part.inline_data.data is read unconditionally into BytesIO and PIL. There is no precondition on size, no upper bound, no error handling for malformed bytes. A malformed or oversized payload from the model raises PIL.UnidentifiedImageError or exhausts memory inside _process_context. The correctness reasoning omits the failure frame entirely. TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best.

issues.description: Example file copyright header and dead system message indicate cargo-culted scaffolding
issues.detail: The example header reads '2024-2025, Daily' while the rest of the repo presumably has a current convention; the on_client_connected handler appends another 'system' message to an already-built context, relying on the aggregator to re-read messages. Neither is wrong per se, but neither is reasoned about in the example's docstring. Minor.

review.summary: The patch adds image-generation support but has not been reasoned about with the discipline its surface area requires. The image-frame construction violates its own declared format contract (RGB vs. PIL's actual mode); a private third-party symbol is monkey-patched at import as a confessed 'temporary hack'; the image-model predicate is a substring match on a vendor naming convention; and the default model is silently changed underneath existing callers. There is no bound or error path on inline image bytes. REFUSED in current form; the fixes are small but the reasoning must be made explicit before merge.
